As of 135 AM Sunday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... Light rain lifting north across central NC will 
linger much of the day before exiting this evening.  

Models have come into somewhat better agreement on placement of QPF 
for today, but amounts still vary quite a bit.  The general 
consensus is that rain that is currently lifting north into and 
across central NC will continue through this morning, perhaps 
increasing a bit in intensity later this morning.  The mostly light 
rain is then expected to linger off-and-on across much of central NC 
through much of the daytime hours today before shifting east, 
exiting and ending this evening when the causative low pressure wave 
offshore exits to the northeast. The QPF possibilities range as low 
as a couple tenths of an inch to as high as an inch and a half, with 
the most likely amount being about a half-inch of rain for many 
locations across central NC. These amounts, and given the lack of 
convection would suggest the rain should be a fairly low-impact 
nature, other than typical wet road concerns.  


KEY MESSAGE 2... A potent storm system may affect much of the 
eastern states including our region Wednesday through Thanksgiving 
Day. Chilly temperatures, gusty NE wind, and some heavy rain may 
target Wednesday afternoon into Thanksgiving morning.

In the wake of the coastal low this weekend, a dry cold front is 
forecast to move across the area Monday night. A strong and chilly 
Canadian high pressure is expected to move east from the upper 
Midwest Tuesday to NY state and New England Wednesday and Thursday. 
A dry and chilly air mass will build down the eastern seaboard into 
the Carolinas Tuesday through early Wednesday as low pressure 
develops off the FL coast. Depending on the timing and strength of 
the approaching mid/upper level trough, the low pressure is forecast 
to move up the coast reaching eastern NC early Thanksgiving Day. 

The latest data suggests a stronger and wetter system for our region 
with the potential for rain to develop by mid-day across southern NC 
spreading quickly north throughout the region by late Wednesday. 
Rain would then be expected Wednesday night and Thursday morning 
with some heavy rainfall possible or even likely. However, models 
suggest several pieces to the mid/upper level features which will no 
doubt have differing responses at the surface. This system is 
expected to be a very dynamic one, with one of more rounds of 
significant rainfall, followed by gusty WNW winds and clearing on the 
backside of the storm Thanksgiving afternoon or evening. 

Current rainfall projections for this mid-week into Thanksgiving 
system are in the 1+ inch range on a widespread basis. However, as 
we have seen with this current system as it evolves, there will be 
some day to day variations within the models in the upcoming days. 

One thing for sure will be the chilly temperatures associates with 
the large and strong high pressure that will build into the region 
from the north Tuesday through Wednesday. A period of strong cold 
air damming (CAD) appears likely Wednesday into Thanksgiving morning 
when NE winds of 15-20 mph with gusts to 25 mph will make it feel 
even colder. Of course, the modeled temperatures may need to be 
adjusted down in the Piedmont if the current thinking remains near 
target for mid-week.

Currently, lows are expected to dip into the lower 30s north to 
around 40 SE Tuesday night. Then, with increasing cloudiness 
Wednesday highs will hold in the upper 40s north and mid 50s south. 
A chilly rain with a gusty NE wind is expected late Wednesday into 
Thanksgiving Day with lows in the mid 30s to mid 40s N to SE and 
highs in the 50s by late day on Thanksgiving (if it clears quickly 
enough). 

Late week could bring the gusty NW winds Friday in the rear of the 
departing storm, with near normal temperatures in the lower to mid 
60s. 

Mainly dry and calm weather is expected Saturday.
